ui.keys: Use ← → to move, Esc to close

intro.title: Drive screen at a glance
body: Monitor and operate the conveyor drives, from the CHARGE POCKET to the DISCHARGE TABLE DRIVE.
Top: operation status, auto-run conditions, time settings / Middle: equipment drawing / Bottom: recent alarms and sensor lamps
Without control permission, 'View only' appears next to the title and buttons and inputs are locked.

opPanel.title: Charge / Discharge OP PANEL
body: Mode (MANUAL/AUTO) shows which way the selector on the field OP panel is set. It cannot be changed from this screen.
When AUTO RUN is lit, the line is running automatically.
When E-STOP lights red [[alarm]], an emergency stop is active.
The DISCHARGE OP PANEL works the same way.

alarmSw.title: ALARM SWITCH
body: ALARM RESET resets alarms; HORN STOP silences the alarm horn.
Hold the button for the hold delay (2 s by default) to activate it. A bar fills under the button while you hold.
The button lights green [[on]] while active and releases when you let go.
It works exactly like the same buttons on the Alarms screen.

cond.title: Charge / Discharge auto-run conditions
body: State of the conditions needed for auto run.
[[on]] Green: met   [[alarm]] Red: not met
If auto run will not start, check the red lamps first.

time.title: Discharge auto-run TIME settings
body: Tap a number to open the number pad; the value (seconds) is applied right away.
Input ranges — Product align (delay) TIME 0–600, Product detect clear TIME 0–600, SIDE CONVEYOR forward TIME 15–50
Values outside the range cannot be entered.

drivePanel.title: Drive control boxes
body: The CHARGE TABLE DRIVE, MAIN/CC DRIVE and DISCHARGE TABLE DRIVE boxes all work the same way.
ON/OFF: hold for the hold delay (2 s by default) to start or stop. A bar fills under the button while you hold.
While running, ON lights green [[on]]; when stopped, OFF lights red [[alarm]].
PV is the current speed; SV is the speed setting. Tap SV to open the number pad (charge and MAIN/CC 0–2610, discharge 0–4110 mm/Min).
DRIVE DETECT NORMAL: green [[on]] means normal, red [[alarm]] means abnormal.

zones.title: MAIN DRIVE zone 1–7 temperatures
body: PV is each zone's current temperature; SV is the set temperature.
Tap SV to open the number pad (0–1000℃). These are the same values as on the Temp Control screen.

facilityOff.title: Equipment OFF temperature
body: The red number is the temperature at which the equipment is switched off.
Each time you hold the OFF button for the hold delay it toggles on/off, and it stays that way after you let go.
Green [[on]] means on; red [[alarm]] means off.

stage.title: Equipment drawing
body: The drawing changes with the equipment state.
Motors: green when running, grey when stopped · Rollers and rails: roll while running · Circulation fans: spin while running
SIDE CONVEYOR arrows: shown only while rising or lowering · DOOR: green [[on]] / red [[alarm]] shows the door state · MAIN zones: orange while active
The rotation detect lamps under the motors and the product detect lamp light green [[on]] when detected.

alarms.title: Recent alarms
body: Shows the latest 100 alarms.
Status 'Active' [[alarm]] means the alarm has not cleared yet; 'Cleared' means it is over.
To search by period or download to Excel, use the Alarm History screen.

boards.title: Sensor and valve lamps
body: Charge/discharge SOL VALVEs, limit switches (L/S), proximity sensors (P/X) and product detection.
[[on]] Green: on / detected   [[alarm]] Red: off

end.title: Good to know
body: The hold delay can be changed on the Engineering screen and applies to every hold button.
You can reopen this guide any time with the ? button at the top right.

intro.title: Combustion screen at a glance
body: Operate the gas, combustion blower and burners, and watch zone 1–7 temperatures and burner state.
Top: equipment drawing (MAIN GAS, COMBUSTION BLOWER, BURNER COOL, zone temperatures and openings) / Middle: per-zone burn controls / Bottom: recent alarms and alarm/PURGE panels
Without control permission, 'View only' appears next to the title and buttons and inputs are locked.

mainGas.title: MAIN GAS
body: Opens and closes the MAIN GAS valve.
Hold OPEN/CLOSE for the hold delay (2 s by default) to operate it. A bar fills under the button while you hold.
When open, OPEN lights green [[on]]; when closed, CLOSE lights red [[alarm]].

pipeLamps.title: Pipe status lamps
body: Status lamps under the pipe fittings: MAIN GAS PRESS NORMAL and SOL SHUT, and COMBUSTION BLOWER PRESS ABNORMAL.
They show the state in green [[on]] / red [[alarm]].

blower.title: COMBUSTION BLOWER
body: Starts and stops the combustion blower.
Hold ON/OFF for the hold delay to operate it.
While running, ON lights green [[on]]; when stopped, OFF lights red [[alarm]].

burnerCool.title: BURNER COOL
body: Turns burner cooling on and off. Hold ON/OFF for the hold delay to operate it.
When on, ON lights green [[on]]; when off, OFF lights red [[alarm]].

zones.title: Zone 1–7 temperatures
body: PV is each zone's current temperature; SV is the set temperature.
Tap SV to open the number pad (0–1000℃). These are the same values as on the Temp Control and Drive screens.

per.title: Zone opening (%)
body: The % boxes above and below each zone show its burner opening (output). Both boxes show the same value.
It is the same value as the output (MV) on the Temp Control screen.

zoneBurn.title: Zone BURN ON/OFF
body: Turns burning on and off for a whole zone. Hold BURN ON/OFF for the hold delay to operate it.
While burning, ON lights green [[on]]; when stopped, OFF lights red [[alarm]].

zoneModal.title: Zone burners
body: Tap 'N ZONE BURNERS' to open the burner window for that zone.
In the window you can turn burners on and off one by one, or purge just that zone. The next pages open the zone 1 window to explain it.

zmBurners.title: Burner window — BURN ON/OFF
body: Each row is one burner, and the zone has as many burners as it has flames.
Like the drawing, they are split into a top row and a bottom row. Numbering starts at the left of the top row and continues from the left of the bottom row.
Hold BURN ON/OFF for the hold delay to turn just that burner on or off.
While burning, BURN ON lights green [[on]]; when stopped, BURN OFF lights red [[alarm]].

zmPurge.title: Burner window — zone PURGE · close
body: Hold START PURGE for the hold delay to purge just this zone. It lights green [[on]] while purging.
Hold STOP PURGE for the hold delay to stop this zone's purge. It lights red [[alarm]] when the stop is active.
Close the window with ✕ at the top right, Esc, or by tapping outside.

stage.title: Equipment drawing
body: The drawing changes with the equipment state.
The MAIN GAS valves and the combustion blower valve and fan keep their own colour when open/running and turn red [[alarm]] when closed/stopped.
The lightning marks behind the flames appear only while igniting.

alarms.title: Recent alarms
body: Shows the latest 100 alarms.
Status 'Active' [[alarm]] means the alarm has not cleared yet; 'Cleared' means it is over.
To search by period or download to Excel, use the Alarm History screen.

alarmReset.title: MISFIRE ALARM · BURNER ALARM
body: MISFIRE lights red [[alarm]] on a misfire, and ABNORMAL lights red [[alarm]] on a burner fault.
Hold RESET for the hold delay to reset that alarm. The RESET buttons are always yellow.

purge.title: ALL PURGE
body: Hold ON for the hold delay to start PURGE for all zones; hold OFF to stop it.
ON lights green [[on]] when active, and OFF lights red [[alarm]] when active.
Progress lights up in order: READY (red [[alarm]]) → PURGING (yellow [[warn]]) → DONE (green [[on]]).

end.title: Good to know
body: The hold delay can be changed on the Engineering screen and applies to every hold button.
You can reopen this guide any time with the ? button at the top right.

intro.title: Temp Control screen at a glance
body: Monitor and set the temperature of zones 1–7, one panel per zone.
All seven panels are laid out the same way. This guide uses the 1ZONE panel.
Without control permission, 'View only' appears next to the title and buttons and inputs are locked.

panel.title: One zone panel
body: Top left: PV, SV and MV bar gauges with their values
Bottom left: AUTO/MANUAL mode button and Manual output (MV)
Right: alarm settings (HH, H, L, LL) and OUTPUT LIMIT

gauges.title: PV · SV · MV
body: PV (red) is the current temperature, SV (green) the set temperature, MV (blue) the output (%).
Tap SV to open the number pad (0–1000℃). It shows the setting in effect, which may move gradually toward your entry.
SV matches the Combustion and Drive screens; MV matches the zone opening (%) on the Combustion screen.

mode.title: AUTO · MANUAL
body: The button shows the current mode: AUTO in green [[on]], MANUAL in red [[alarm]].
In AUTO, the output (MV) is set automatically to reach the set temperature (SV).
Hold the button for the hold delay (2 s by default) to switch modes. A bar fills under the button while you hold.

manualMv.title: Manual output (MV)
body: Sets the output (%) directly in MANUAL mode. Tap the box to open the number pad (0–100%).
In AUTO mode the box is dimmed and locked.

alarm.title: Alarm settings HH · H · L · LL
body: HH, H, L and LL are the reference values for the high-high, high, low and low-low alarms.
Tap a box to open the number pad. Input ranges — HH 0–500, H 0–200, L 0–200, LL 0–400
Values outside the range cannot be entered.

limit.title: OUTPUT LIMIT (MV%)
body: Sets the range the output (MV) can move in. The output never goes below Low or above High.
Tap a box to open the number pad (High and Low both 0–100%).

end.title: Good to know
body: 2–7ZONE panels work exactly like 1ZONE. Each panel's values apply only to its own zone.
The hold delay can be changed on the Engineering screen and applies to every hold button.
You can reopen this guide any time with the ? button at the top right.

intro.title: Atmosphere screen at a glance
body: Monitor and operate the ADDITION BLOWER and GAS lines and the ADDITION CONTROL MOTOR VALVE.
Top left: ADDITION BLOWER/GAS / Center: control valve panel / Bottom left: auto-mode conditions / Right: generator, to furnace, O2 SENSOR
Without control permission, 'View only' appears next to the title and buttons and inputs are locked.

addition.title: ADDITION BLOWER · GAS
body: Hold OPEN/CLOSE for the hold delay (2 s by default) to operate it. A bar fills under the button while you hold.
When open, OPEN lights green [[on]]; when closed, CLOSE lights red [[alarm]].
It stays that way after you let go. To change it, hold the other button.

pipeLamps.title: PRESS ABNORMAL · SOL SHUT
body: Status lamps under the pressure control valves and solenoid valves.
They show the state in green [[on]] / red [[alarm]].

fittings.title: Equipment drawing
body: The drawing changes with the equipment state.
Blower, pressure control valves, solenoid valves: green [[on]] when operating, grey [[off]] otherwise
Control valve on the main pipe: spins while operating · Beacon above the generator: shows the state in green [[on]] / red [[alarm]].

valveValues.title: Control valve — PV · SV · MV
body: PV (red) is the current value; MV (orange) is the output (%).
SV (green) is the set value. Tap it to open the number pad (0–1200 mmV).

pid.title: Control valve — P · I · D
body: Control settings that decide the output in AUTO. P is the proportional band, I the integral time, D the derivative time.
Tap a box to open the number pad. Input ranges — P 0–1200, I 0–2400, D 0–600

refTemp.title: Allowed ref. temp
body: Tap the box to open the number pad (650–1000℃).
When the temperature reaches the allowed reference temperature, the lamp on the left lights green [[on]]. It is one of the auto-mode conditions.

mode.title: AUTO · MANUAL
body: The current mode lights green [[on]].
Hold the mode you want for the hold delay to switch to it; it stays after you let go.
In AUTO, the output (MV) is set automatically to reach the set value (SV).

manualMv.title: MANUAL MV (manual output)
body: Sets the output (%) directly in MANUAL mode. Tap the box to open the number pad (0–100%).
In AUTO mode the box is dimmed and locked.

cond.title: Auto-mode conditions
body: The seven conditions needed for atmosphere control to run in AUTO.
[[on]] Green: met   [[alarm]] Red: not met
If AUTO will not run, check the red lamps first.

gen.title: GENERATOR
body: When the generator GAS is open, OPEN lights green [[on]]; when closed, CLOSE lights red [[alarm]].
It cannot be opened or closed from this screen.

o2.title: O2 SENSOR
body: The O2 sensor value inside the furnace (mmV).

end.title: Good to know
body: The hold delay can be changed on the Engineering screen and applies to every hold button.
You can reopen this guide any time with the ? button at the top right.

intro.title: Cooling screen at a glance
body: Monitor how the cooling water circulates and set the cooling alarm delay.
The water flows from the tank under the tower → cooling pumps → COOLING CHAMBER → sump → circulation pumps → cooling tower.
Without control permission, 'View only' appears next to the title and inputs are locked.

motor.title: Cooling tower top motor
body: It turns green [[on]] while running and keeps its normal colour when stopped.

pumps.title: Cooling pumps · circulation pumps
body: The two in the middle are NO.1/NO.2 COOLING PUMP; the two at the bottom left are NO.1/NO.2 CIRC. PUMP.
They turn green [[on]] while running and keep their normal colour when stopped.

arrows.title: Cooling water flow arrows
body: The arrows blink on pipes where cooling water is flowing. They stay still when there is no flow.
The arrow points in the direction the water flows.

level.title: SUMP LEVEL HIGH · LOW
body: When the sump level is high, a red 'SUMP LEVEL HIGH' band appears in the sump; when low, 'SUMP LEVEL LOW'.
Normally no band is shown.
[[ex]]The two bands marked 'Example' are shown for this guide because there is no alarm right now.

delay.title: COOLING ALARM DELAY
body: The alarm delay (minutes) for HIGH and LOW.
Tap a box to open the number pad. Enter 0 or more.

end.title: Good to know
body: Nothing is switched on or off from this screen. The pumps, motor and arrows show the equipment state.
You can reopen this guide any time with the ? button at the top right.

intro.title: Trend screen at a glance
body: See how the zone 1–7 temperatures and the O2 value changed over time, as a chart.
Top: period, auto refresh, memos, downloads / Center: chart / Right: values and line switches
When opened it shows the last 24 hours with auto refresh on.

period.title: Period search
body: Pick the start and end time and press [Search] to draw that period.
Picking a date yourself turns auto refresh off.

quick.title: Quick periods
body: Shows the last 1, 3, 6, 12 or 24 hours right away. The period boxes above are filled in too.
The button for the period you are viewing is lit. Pressing one turns auto refresh off.

follow.title: Auto Refresh
body: While on ('Refreshing'), the last 24 hours are redrawn every 30 seconds so the chart keeps up with now.
Setting a period yourself turns it off. Press it again to turn it back on and return to the last 24 hours.

memo.title: Memos
body: [Add Memo] opens a window. Enter the time, title and text and save — a memo card appears on the chart at that time.
Tap a card to edit or delete it. The number of memos in this period is shown next to the button.

export.title: Export Excel · Save Chart
body: Export Excel: saves the values of the lines that are switched on, for the period you searched.
Save Chart: saves the chart you are looking at as a PNG image. Memo cards are not included.
Files go to this PC's Downloads folder and are also saved on the server PC under D:\온도데이터, in the '엑셀 내려받기' and '트렌드 저장' folders.

chart.title: Chart
body: Zone 1–7 temperatures use the right axis (℃); O2 uses the left axis (mmV).
Hover over the chart to see every value at that time.

values.title: End values
body: The last value in the period you searched. The number has the same colour as its line.
If you search a past period, you see the values at the end of that period.

toggle.title: Line on/off
body: Tap a switch to hide or show that line on the chart.
Only lines that are on go into Export Excel.

focus.title: View by this line's range
body: Tap a name (1ZONE, O2, …) to set that line's axis to its own range so small changes show clearly. The name gets underlined.
Tap it again to go back to the default range.

range.title: Line ranges
body: The min–max used by 'view by this line's range'. Saved ranges look bright; default ranges look dim.
With control permission, tap one to change the min and max, or press [Use Default]. Changes reach the other PCs too.

end.title: Good to know
body: Temperature data is saved automatically every day as an Excel file (온도데이터_date.xlsx) on the server PC in D:\온도데이터\일일온도데이터.
You can reopen this guide any time with the ? button at the top right.

intro.title: Alarms screen at a glance
body: Lays out the equipment alarms as tiles and shows active alarms in red.
Top: page buttons, ALARM RESET, HORN STOP, active count / Below: alarm tiles (100 per page)
Without control permission the buttons are locked. You can still tap a tile to view its description and files.

pager.title: Pages
body: There are more than 100 alarms, so they are split into pages. Tap a number or the ‹ › arrows to change page.
Next to them is the address range of the alarms on this page.

cells.title: Alarm tiles
body: An active alarm lights its tile red [[alarm]]; when it clears, the tile goes back to normal.
A tile with a paperclip in the top-right corner has a description or files.
[[ex]]The first three tiles marked 'Example' are shown for this guide because no alarm is active on this page.

count.title: Active count
body: The number of alarms active right now, counting every page.
It turns red [[alarm]] when there is at least one.

actions.title: ALARM RESET · HORN STOP
body: ALARM RESET resets alarms; HORN STOP silences the alarm horn.
Hold the button for the hold delay (2 s by default) to activate it. A bar fills under the button while you hold.
The button lights green [[on]] while active and releases when you let go. It works exactly like the same buttons on the Drive screen.

open.title: Alarm description · files window
body: Tap an alarm tile to open its description, photo and PDF window.
The next pages open the first tile's window to explain it.

desc.title: Description
body: Write the cause, corrective action, etc. for the alarm here (up to 255 characters), then press [Save].
Without control permission you can only read the description.

files.title: Photo · PDF · close
body: You can upload one photo (JPG/PNG) and one PDF (up to 20MB each). Manage them with [Upload], [Replace] and [Delete].
Tap the photo to see it at full size; press [Open] to open the PDF in a new tab.
Close the window with ✕ at the top right, [Close], Esc, or by tapping outside.

end.title: Good to know
body: To see only the alarms active right now, use the Active Alarms screen; to search past alarms by period, use the Alarm History screen.
The hold delay can be changed on the Engineering screen and applies to every hold button.
You can reopen this guide any time with the ? button at the top right.

intro.title: Active Alarms screen at a glance
body: Collects only the alarms that are active right now. It is a view-only screen with no buttons to press.
Left: alarm history entries not yet cleared / Right: tiles lit red on the Alarms screen
Left open, it refreshes by itself. There is no need to press Search.

hist.title: Active alarm table
body: Columns are NO, Tag Name, Address, Alarm Message and Occurred; the most recent alarm is at the top.
When an alarm clears it leaves the table. Over 20 entries, use the pages under the table.
To search cleared alarms by period too, use the Alarm History screen.

lamps.title: Lit alarm tiles
body: Shows only the tiles lit red on the Alarms screen. Top: alarm message; bottom: tag name and address.
They are in the same order as the table on the left so you can match them easily. With none lit, 'No lamps are on.' is shown.
[[ex]]The three tiles marked 'Example' are shown for this guide because no tile is lit right now.

counts.title: Active counts
body: The count for each side. It turns red [[alarm]] when there is at least one.
A new alarm appears on the right first and shows up in the table on the left a few seconds later.

end.title: Good to know
body: To reset alarms (ALARM RESET) or silence the horn (HORN STOP), use the buttons on the Alarms or Drive screen.
You can reopen this guide any time with the ? button at the top right.

intro.title: Alarm History screen at a glance
body: Find past alarms by the time they occurred and download them to Excel. Cleared alarms are kept too.
When opened it shows the whole history with no period set.
It does not refresh by itself. Press [Search] again to see new alarms.

period.title: Occurred period
body: Pick the start and end time and press [Search] (or Enter in a box) to load the alarms that occurred in between.
You can pick the year and month at the top of the calendar, and clear a box with its ✕. A cleared side has no limit.

count.title: Count
body: The total number of alarms loaded. While loading it shows 'Loading'.

filter.title: Header search boxes
body: Type into the Tag Name, Address or Alarm Message box to keep only the loaded rows that contain that text.
For Status, choose All, Active or Cleared.
This narrows the list already loaded; it does not change the period.

table.title: Alarm list
body: Status shows Active in red [[alarm]] and Cleared in grey [[off]]; cleared alarms also show the Cleared time.
Tap a column title to sort by it. Each page has 20 rows; use the buttons under the table to change page.

excel.title: Export Excel
body: Downloads exactly what the table shows now (including header-box filters and sort order) as an Excel file.
The file goes to this PC's Downloads folder. It cannot be pressed when no alarms are loaded.

end.title: Good to know
body: To watch only the alarms active right now, refreshing by itself, use the Active Alarms screen.
You can reopen this guide any time with the ? button at the top right.

intro.title: Log screen at a glance
body: A record of values sent to the equipment with the buttons and input boxes on the screens: who sent which value to which address (which tag), when, and whether it succeeded.
When opened it shows the whole log with no period set, newest first.
It does not refresh by itself. Press [Search] again to see new records.

period.title: Logged period
body: Pick the start and end time and press [Search] (or Enter in a box) to load the records in between.
You can pick the year and month at the top of the calendar, and clear a box with its ✕. A cleared side has no limit.

count.title: Count
body: The total number of records loaded. While loading it shows 'Loading'.

filter.title: Header search boxes
body: Type into the Name, Address, Description or Value Sent box to keep only the loaded rows that contain that text.
For Result choose All, OK or Failed; for Failure Reason choose a kind of failure.
This narrows the list already loaded; it does not change the period.

table.title: Operation log
body: Description says what the tag is; it is kept as it was when the value was sent. Records from before descriptions existed, and tags without one, show '—'.
Result shows OK in green [[on]] and Failed in red [[alarm]]. Old records from before results were kept show '—'.
Failed records also show a Failure Reason (Connection failed, Timed out, Server error, Write rejected, No response).
Tap a column title to sort by it. Each page has 20 rows; use the buttons under the table to change page.

excel.title: Export Excel
body: Downloads exactly what the table shows now (including header-box filters and sort order) as an Excel file.
The file goes to this PC's Downloads folder. It cannot be pressed when no records are loaded.

end.title: Good to know
body: A button released before the hold delay is up sends no value, so it is not logged.
Changes to Operation Settings on the Engineering screen (hold delay, login time limit) are not logged here.
You can reopen this guide any time with the ? button at the top right.

intro.title: Engineering screen at a glance
body: Change equipment settings and how the screens are operated. Use the tabs at the top to switch between General and Burner Control (zones 1–4, 5–7).
This guide covers the Operation Settings panel on the General tab.
Without control permission, 'View only' appears next to the title and inputs are locked.

operation.title: Operation Settings
body: Settings for how the screens are used. Tap a box to open the number pad; the value is saved right away.
A change applies not only to this PC but to every PC and every user.

hold.title: Button hold delay
body: Control buttons on every screen (ON/OFF, OPEN/CLOSE, RESET, …) must be held this long to act. This stops equipment from moving on an accidental touch.
Enter 0–5 s in 0.1 s steps (2 s by default). At 0 a button acts as soon as it is pressed.
Other PCs pick it up when they change screen or within 30 seconds.

session.title: Login time limit
body: Once this time has passed since login, the screen returns to the login page and the user must log in again.
Enter minutes. 0 means unlimited; the maximum is 1440 min (24 h).

end.title: Good to know
body: Drive, Combustion and Atmosphere Settings and Temperature Calibration will be added to this guide once their items are settled.
You can reopen this guide any time with the ? button at the top right.
